questions.text: A shaft subjected to pure torsion develops a maximum shear stress of 100 MPa. The yield strength of the material in uniaxial tension is 300 MPa. According to the Maximum Shear Stress Theory (Tresca), the factor of safety is:
questions.solution: Shortcut: For pure torsion, max shear stress τ_max = τ. Tresca criterion: τ_max = S_yt / (2 × FS). Thus FS = S_yt / (2 × τ_max) = 300 / (2 × 100) = 1.5. Full Solution: Pure torsion stress state: σ₁ = τ, σ₂ = 0, σ₃ = -τ. Max shear stress = (σ₁ - σ₃)/2 = τ = 100 MPa. Yielding occurs when max shear stress = S_yt/2 = 150 MPa. Factor of Safety = Yield Shear Stress / Working Shear Stress = 150 / 100 = 1.5.
questions.topic: Strength of Materials - Theories of Failure

questions.text: A helical spring of stiffness k is cut into two equal halves. The same mass m is attached to one of the halves. The ratio of the new natural frequency to the original natural frequency is:
questions.solution: Shortcut: Spring stiffness is inversely proportional to its length; halving the length doubles the stiffness (k' = 2k). Since natural frequency ω ∝ √k, the new frequency becomes √2 times the original. Full solution: Original ω = √(k/m). After cutting, each half has stiffness 2k. New ω' = √(2k/m) = √2 √(k/m) = √2 ω. Hence the ratio is √2.

questions.text: A centrifugal pump running at 1500 rpm delivers 0.1 m³/saga inst a head of 30 m. If the speed is increased to 1800 rpm, the new discharge (m³/s) and head (m) respectively, assuming affinity laws hold, are:
questions.solution: Shortcut: Affinity laws: Q ∝ N, H ∝ N². Speed ratio = 1800/1500 = 1.2. Q₂ = 0.1 × 1.2 = 0.12 m³/s. H₂ = 30 × (1.2)² = 30 × 1.44 = 43.2 m. Full: Q₂/Q₁ = N₂/N₁ → Q₂ = 0.1(1800/1500) = 0.12. H₂/H₁ = (N₂/N₁)² → H₂ = 30(1.2)² = 43.2.

questions.text: In a vapor compression refrigeration cycle, the enthalpy at compressor inlet is 250 kJ/kg, at compressor outlet is 280 kJ/kg, and at condenser outlet is 100 kJ/kg. The throttling process is isenthalpic. The COP of the cycle is:
questions.solution: Shortcut: COP = (h₁ - h₄)/(h₂ - h₁). Since throttling is isenthalpic, h₄ = h₃ = 100 kJ/kg. RE = 250 - 100 = 150 kJ/kg. WC = 280 - 250 = 30 kJ/kg. COP = 150/30 = 5.0. Full method: Refrigeration effect q_L = h₁ - h₄ = 250 - 100 = 150 kJ/kg. Compressor work w_c = h₂ - h₁ = 280 - 250 = 30 kJ/kg. COP_R = q_L/w_c = 150/30 = 5.0.

questions.text: A solid circular shaft transmits 80 kW at 1000 rpm. The allowable shear stress is 40 MPa. The required shaft diameter (in mm) is approximately:
questions.solution: Shortcut: Torque T = 9550·P(kW)/N(rpm) = 9550·80/1000 = 764 Nm. Diameter from τ = 16T/(πd^3) → d^3 = 16·764/(π·40×10^6) ≈ 9.73×10^-5 m^3 → d ≈ 0.0458 m ≈ 50 mm. Full solution: Compute torque, then solve torsion formula for d.

questions.text: The table shows the measured resistances of a copper wire at three temperatures. | Temperature (°C) | Resistance (Ω) | |------------------|----------------| | 20 | 1.00 | | 60 | 1.20 | | 100 | 1.40 | Using the linear temperature coefficient shortcut R = R₀[1+αΔT], estimate the resistance at 80 °C:
questions.topic: Electrical engineering – temperature coefficient of resistance

questions.text: In a machining operation, the tool life is 60 minutes at a cutting speed of 100 m/min. If the Taylor's exponent n = 0.5, what is the tool life (in minutes) at a cutting speed of 200 m/min?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Taylor's tool life equation V·T^n = constant. Since n = 0.5, T ∝ 1/V^2. Doubling V reduces T by factor 4: 60/4 = 15 min. Full solution: C = 100 × 60^0.5 = 100 × 7.746 = 774.6. At V=200, T = (C/200)^(1/0.5) = (3.873)^2 = 15 min.

questions.text: What is the unit digit of 7^2023?
questions.solution: Shortcut: The unit digit of powers of 7 follows a cycle of 4: 7, 9, 3, 1. Since 2023 mod 4 = 3, the unit digit is the 3rd in the cycle, which is 3. Full solution: 7^1=7, 7^2=49, 7^3=343, 7^4=2401; the pattern repeats every 4. 2023 = 4×505 + 3, so unit digit of 7^2023 equals unit digit of 7^3 = 3.

questions.text: In a parallel flow heat exchanger, the hot fluid enters at 120°C and leaves at 80°C. The cold fluid enters at 30°C and leaves at 60°C. The log mean temperature difference (LMTD) in °C is:
questions.solution: Shortcut: For parallel flow, ΔT₁ = T_h,in - T_c,in = 90°C, ΔT₂ = T_h,out - T_c,out = 20°C. LMTD = (ΔT₁ - ΔT₂)/ln(ΔT₁/ΔT₂) = 70/ln(4.5) ≈ 70/1.504 ≈ 46.5°C. Full method: ΔT₁ = 120 - 30 = 90°C. ΔT₂ = 80 - 60 = 20°C. LMTD = (90 - 20)/ln(90/20) = 70/ln(4.5) = 70/1.504077 = 46.54°C ≈ 46.5°C.

questions.text: In a certain code language, 'TABLE' is written as 'UBCMF'. How is 'CHAIR' written in that code?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Each letter in the code is shifted forward by one position in the alphabet (Caesar cipher +1). Applying this to CHAIR gives C→D, H→I, A→B, I→J, R→S → DIBJS. Full solution: Comparing TABLE and UBCMF shows T→U, A→B, B→C, L→M, E→F, confirming a uniform +1 shift. Using the same rule on CHAIR yields DIBJS.

questions.text: As per the table, a heat engine operates between a source at 1000 K and a sink at 300 K. The heat input is 500 kJ and the work output is 200 kJ. The second law efficiency of the engine is:
questions.solution: Shortcut: Second law efficiency = (Actual thermal efficiency) / (Carnot efficiency). Actual efficiency = 200/500 = 0.4. Carnot efficiency = 1 - 300/1000 = 0.7. Ratio = 0.4/0.7 ≈ 0.571. Full solution: Carnot efficiency η_C = 1 - T_L/T_H = 1 - 300/1000 = 0.7. Actual efficiency η = W/Q_H = 200/500 = 0.4. Second law efficiency η_II = η/η_C = 0.4/0.7 = 0.571 ≈ 0.57.

questions.text: Heat Q = 1000 kJ is transferred from a reservoir at 500 K to another at 300 K. The ambient temperature is 300 K. The exergy destruction (in kJ) during this process is:
questions.solution: Shortcut: Exergy destruction = T₀ × Q × (1/T_L - 1/T_H) = 300 × 1000 × (1/300 - 1/500) = 300 × 1000 × (2/1500) = 400 kJ. Full Solution: Entropy generation S_gen = Q/T_L - Q/T_H = 1000/300 - 1000/500 = 10/3 - 2 = 4/3 kJ/K. Exergy destruction (Irreversibility) I = T₀ × S_gen = 300 × (4/3) = 400 kJ.

questions.text: A long cylindrical fin of diameter 5 mm and thermal conductivity 200 W/m·K is exposed to a convection environment with h = 50 W/m²·K. Using the infinite fin approximation, the fin effectiveness is approximately:
questions.solution: Shortcut: For a long fin, effectiveness ε = √(kP/hAc). For a cylinder, P/Ac = 4/d. Thus ε = 2√(k/hd) = 2√(200/(50×0.005)) = 2√800 ≈ 56.6. Full: m = √(hP/kAc) = √(4h/kd) = √(4×50/(200×0.005)) = √200 ≈ 14.14 m⁻¹. mL = 14.14×0.1 = 1.414. Although mL < 2.65, the problem states 'infinite fin approximation'. Effectiveness ε = √(kP/hAc) = √(k×(πd)/(h×πd²/4)) = √(4k/hd) = 2√(200/(50×0.005)) = 2√800 = 56.57 ≈ 56.

questions.text: A rotor with a moment of inertia of 0.5 kg·m² spins at 300 rad/s. The shaft precesses at 10 rad/s. If the spin speed is doubled and the precession speed is halved, the new gyroscopic couple (in N·m) will be:
questions.solution: Shortcut: Gyroscopic couple C = I·ω·ω_p. The product ω·ω_p changes by factor (2)×(0.5)=1, so couple remains unchanged at 1500 N·m. Step-by-step: Original couple = 0.5 × 300 × 10 = 1500 N·m. New spin = 600 rad/s, new precession = 5 rad/s. New couple = 0.5 × 600 × 5 = 1500 N·m.

questions.text: A simply supported beam of span L carries a uniformly distributed load w over its entire length. The same beam carries a central point load equal to the total distributed load (W = wL). The ratio of the maximum deflection under UDL to that under the central point load is:
questions.solution: Shortcut: Known formula ratio δ_udl/δ_point = (5/384)/(1/48) = 5/8. Full solution: δ_udl = 5wL^4/(384EI), δ_point = (wL)L^3/(48EI) = wL^4/(48EI). Ratio = (5/384)/(1/48) = 5/8.
